chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The closest state of the servant to disbelief is that a man establishes brotherhood with another man upon the Religion, so he counts against him his slips and his mistakes in order to rebuke him with them one day.
ai.seo_question: What is the closest state to disbelief in social relations among believers?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi warns that maintaining a mental ledger of a brother's minor linguistic slips (zillat) for future reproach transforms social intimacy into a source of spiritual vulnerability, bringing one perilously close to kufr. This concept underscores the importance of 'satr' (concealing faults) in communal bonds, contrasting the critical eye of the self-righteous with the merciful disposition of the faithful. It serves as a practical guideline for maintaining humility and preventing the erosion of brotherhood through nitpicking.
